chapterTitle: The Beast from the Sea and the Beast from the Land
themeTitle: “Here Is the Endurance and the Faith of the Saints”

scripture.text: Then I stood on the sand of the sea. I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads. On his horns were ten crowns, and on his heads, blasphemous names.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον τῆς θαλάσσης, “Then I stood on the sand of the sea” — many manuscripts read ‘he stood’: the dragon takes his stand on the shore to summon his helper. καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον, “I saw a beast coming up out of the sea” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); θηρίον, a wild, dangerous animal, as distinct from ζῷον, the living creatures of the throne (4:6). In Daniel 7 four beasts rise from the sea: four empires. To John's readers, Rome came from across the sea. ἔχων κέρατα δέκα καὶ κεφαλὰς ἑπτά, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν κεράτων αὐτοῦ δέκα διαδήματα, “having ten horns and seven heads. On his horns were ten crowns” — διάδημα, from the crown family: royal crowns, like the dragon's (12:3). καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ὀνόματα βλασφημίας, “and on his heads, blasphemous names” — emperors took titles such as ‘divine’, ‘son of god’ and ‘lord’.

scripture.text: The beast which I saw was like a leopard, and his feet were like those of a bear, and his mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon gave him his power, his throne, and great authority.
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδον ἦν ὅμοιον παρδάλει, “The beast which I saw was like a leopard” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς ἄρκου, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ὡς στόμα λέοντος, “and his feet were like those of a bear, and his mouth like the mouth of a lion” — Daniel's first three beasts (lion, bear, leopard) combined in one: this beast sums up all the oppressive empires of history. καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ δράκων τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην, “The dragon gave him his power, his throne, and great authority” — δύναμις and ἐξουσία, two members of the power family: ability and authority, both on loan from Satan. It is the offer Jesus refused in the wilderness.

scripture.text: One of his heads looked like it had been wounded fatally. His fatal wound was healed, and the whole earth marveled at the beast.
scripture.understanding: καὶ μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεφαλῶν αὐτοῦ ὡς ἐσφαγμένην εἰς θάνατον, “One of his heads looked like it had been wounded fatally” — σφάζω, the word used of the Lamb ‘as though it had been slain’ (5:6): the beast is a counterfeit Christ, with a counterfeit death. καὶ ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐθεραπεύθη, “His fatal wound was healed” — θεραπεύω, from the heal family: to restore, to cure — a counterfeit resurrection. Many see the Roman Empire's recovery after Nero's suicide and the chaos of AD 69; there were also rumours that Nero would return. καὶ ἐθαυμάσθη ὅλη ἡ γῆ ὀπίσω τοῦ θηρίου, “and the whole earth marveled at the beast” — γῆ, from the world family: the world follows what impresses it.

scripture.text: They worshiped the dragon, because he gave his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, “Who is like the beast? Who is able to make war with him?”
scripture.understanding: καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ δράκοντι ὅτι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τῷ θηρίῳ, “They worshiped the dragon, because he gave his authority to the beast” — προσκυνέω; ἐξουσία, from the power family. Worship of the state is worship of Satan behind it. καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ λέγοντες· Τίς ὅμοιος τῷ θηρίῳ; “and they worshiped the beast, saying, ‘Who is like the beast?’” — a parody of Israel's song, ‘Who is like you, LORD?’ and of Michael's name, ‘Who is like God?’ καὶ τίς δύναται πολεμῆσαι μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ; “Who is able to make war with him?” — δύναμαι, from the power family: the world worships power.

scripture.text: A mouth speaking great things and blasphemy was given to him. Authority to make war for forty-two months was given to him.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας, “A mouth speaking great things and blasphemy was given to him” — Daniel's little horn ‘had a mouth speaking great things’. ‘Was given’: the passive appears again and again in this chapter — the beast acts only because God permits it. καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ποιῆσαι μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο, “Authority to make war for forty-two months was given to him” — ἐξουσία, from the power family; μήν, from the time family: the same period as the trampling of the holy city and the witness of the two prophets (11:2–3). His time is fixed and short.

scripture.text: He opened his mouth for blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his dwelling, those who dwell in heaven.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εἰς βλασφημίας πρὸς τὸν θεόν, “He opened his mouth for blasphemy against God” — βλασφημία, slander against God. βλασφημῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας, “to blaspheme his name, and his dwelling, those who dwell in heaven” — σκηνή and σκηνόω, tent and tabernacling: God's dwelling is His people, who belong to heaven even while on earth (12:12).

scripture.text: It was given to him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them. Authority over every tribe, people, language, and nation was given to him.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων καὶ νικῆσαι αὐτούς, “It was given to him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them” — νικάω: as with the two witnesses (11:7), the beast ‘overcomes’ the saints by killing them; but in God's eyes they overcome him by dying faithfully (12:11; 15:2). καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν φυλὴν καὶ λαὸν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ ἔθνος, “Authority over every tribe, people, language, and nation was given to him” — ἐξουσία, from the power family: a counterfeit of the Lamb's people from every tribe (5:9). ἅγιος is from the holy family — holy, set apart for God; as a noun, the saints — God’s holy people.

scripture.text: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who has been killed.
scripture.understanding: καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, “All who dwell on the earth will worship him” — γῆ, from the world family: the earth-dwellers, as distinct from those who dwell in heaven (v. 6). οὗ οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου τοῦ ἐσφαγμένου ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, “everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who has been killed” — βιβλίον, from the book family; ζωή, from the life family; ἀρνίον, from the lamb family; κόσμος, from the world family. ‘From the foundation of the world’ may go with ‘written’ (as in 17:8) or with ‘killed’ — the cross was God's plan before creation (1 Peter 1:20). Either way, God's people are known and kept from eternity.

scripture.text: If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
scripture.understanding: Εἴ τις ἔχει οὖς ἀκουσάτω, “If anyone has an ear, let him hear” — the refrain of the seven letters (2:7), now without ‘what the Spirit says to the assemblies’: this chapter is the test the churches were being prepared for.

scripture.text: If anyone is to go into captivity, he will go into captivity. If anyone is to be killed with the sword, he must be killed. Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.
scripture.understanding: εἴ τις εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν, εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν ὑπάγει, “If anyone is to go into captivity, he will go into captivity” — echoing Jeremiah: what God has appointed will happen. εἴ τις ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι, αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι, “If anyone is to be killed with the sword, he must be killed” — μάχαιρα, from the sword family: the state's sword. Believers are not to fight back with the beast's weapons (Matthew 26:52). Ὧδέ ἐστιν ἡ ὑπομονὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις τῶν ἁγίων, “Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints” — ὑπομονή, from the endurance family: remaining under pressure; πίστις, faithfulness. The saints' response to the beast is not violence or panic but faithful endurance. ἅγιος is from the holy family — holy, set apart for God; as a noun, the saints — God’s holy people.

scripture.text: I saw another beast coming up out of the earth. He had two horns like a lamb, and he spoke like a dragon.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς γῆς, “I saw another beast coming up out of the earth” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); ἄλλος, from the another family: another of the same kind, a partner of the first; γῆ, from the world family. Later he is called ‘the false prophet’ (16:13; 19:20). καὶ εἶχεν κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ, “He had two horns like a lamb” — ἀρνίον, from the lamb family: he looks gentle, religious, Christ-like. Jesus warned of false prophets ‘in sheep’s clothing’. καὶ ἐλάλει ὡς δράκων, “and he spoke like a dragon” — his words reveal his master.

scripture.text: He exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence. He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose fatal wound was healed.
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πρώτου θηρίου πᾶσαν ποιεῖ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, “He exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence” — ἐξουσία, from the power family. In John's world, the local priests and councils of the imperial cult enforced emperor-worship in every city of Asia. καὶ ποιεῖ τὴν γῆν καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικοῦντας ἵνα προσκυνήσουσιν τὸ θηρίον τὸ πρῶτον, “He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast” — γῆ, from the world family. Religion serving political power. οὗ ἐθεραπεύθη ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, “whose fatal wound was healed” — θεραπεύω, from the heal family.

scripture.text: He performs great signs, even making fire come down out of the sky to the earth in the sight of people.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ποιεῖ σημεῖα μεγάλα, “He performs great signs” — σημεῖον, from the signs family: counterfeit miracles. Jesus warned that false prophets would ‘show great signs and wonders’. ἵνα καὶ πῦρ ποιῇ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνειν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, “even making fire come down out of the sky to the earth in the sight of people” — imitating Elijah and the two witnesses (11:5); γῆ, from the world family. Miracles alone prove nothing; the test is whether they lead to the worship of God.

scripture.text: He deceives my own people who dwell on the earth because of the signs he was granted to do in front of the beast; saying to those who dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast who had the sword wound and lived.
scripture.understanding: καὶ πλανᾷ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς διὰ τὰ σημεῖα, “He deceives my own people who dwell on the earth because of the signs” — πλανάω, to lead astray: the very work of the dragon, ‘the deceiver of the whole world’; γῆ, from the world family; σημεῖον, from the signs family. (Most manuscripts read simply ‘those who dwell on the earth’.) λέγων τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ποιῆσαι εἰκόνα τῷ θηρίῳ, “saying to those who dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast” — εἰκών, from the image family: a statue, a representation, as distinct from ὁμοίωμα, a mere likeness. Temples to the emperors stood in Ephesus, Pergamum and Smyrna, with images before which citizens burned incense. ὃς ἔχει τὴν πληγὴν τῆς μαχαίρης καὶ ἔζησεν, “who had the sword wound and lived” — μάχαιρα, from the sword family; ζάω, from the life family: the beast's counterfeit resurrection again.

scripture.text: It was given to him to give breath to it, to the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause as many as wouldn’t worship the image of the beast to be killed.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ δοῦναι πνεῦμα τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου, “It was given to him to give breath to it, to the image of the beast” — πνεῦμα, breath; εἰκών, from the image family. Trickery with speaking statues was known in pagan temples; and every idol is given ‘life’ by the devotion of its worshippers. A grim parody of the breath of life entering the witnesses (11:11). ἵνα καὶ λαλήσῃ ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ θηρίου, καὶ ποιήσῃ ἵνα ὅσοι ἐὰν μὴ προσκυνήσωσιν τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου ἀποκτανθῶσιν, “that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause as many as wouldn’t worship the image of the beast to be killed” — εἰκών three times. Like Nebuchadnezzar's golden image (Daniel 3): bow or die.

scripture.text: He causes all, the small and the great, the rich and the poor, and the free and the slave, to be given marks on their right hands, or on their foreheads;
scripture.understanding: καὶ ποιεῖ πάντας, τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς, καὶ τοὺς ἐλευθέρους καὶ τοὺς δούλους, “He causes all, the small and the great, the rich and the poor, and the free and the slave” — δοῦλος, from the servant family: no class escapes. ἵνα δῶσιν αὐτοῖς χάραγμα ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς ἢ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῶν, “to be given marks on their right hands, or on their foreheads” — χάραγμα, an engraved stamp: the word for the emperor's image stamped on coins and documents, and for the brand on a slave. It is the beast's counterfeit of God's seal on His servants' foreheads (7:3). The strongest reading is that it marks allegiance — in thought (forehead) and action (hand); many expect also a literal mark at the end.

scripture.text: and that no one would be able to buy or to sell, unless he has that mark, the name of the beast or the number of his name.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἵνα μή τις δύνηται ἀγοράσαι ἢ πωλῆσαι, “and that no one would be able to buy or to sell” — δύναμαι, from the power family; ἀγοράζω, from the redeem family: the same verb used of the Lamb ‘buying’ people for God (5:9). The beast controls the marketplace; the Lamb buys people out of it. In Asia, trade guilds required honouring the gods and the emperor; refusing could cost your livelihood. εἰ μὴ ὁ ἔχων τὸ χάραγμα, τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θηρίου ἢ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ, “unless he has that mark, the name of the beast or the number of his name.”

scripture.text: Here is wisdom. He who has understanding, let him calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man. His number is six hundred sixty-six.
scripture.understanding: Ὧδε ἡ σοφία ἐστίν, “Here is wisdom” — σοφία, from the wisdom family: not cleverness for puzzles, but the discernment to see through the beast. ὁ ἔχων νοῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου, “He who has understanding, let him calculate the number of the beast” — νοῦς, the mind; ψηφίζω, to count with pebbles. In Greek and Hebrew, letters were also numbers, so names could be added up. ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν, “for it is the number of a man” — a human number, or the number of a particular man. καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτοῦ ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ, “His number is six hundred sixty-six” — ‘Nero Caesar’ written in Hebrew letters adds up to 666, and some manuscripts read 616, which matches the Latin spelling — a strong sign that early readers thought of Nero. Many also see 6, one short of the perfect 7, tripled: humanity's best attempt at deity, always falling short. Both may be meant: the beast is a Nero-like ruler and every power that sets itself up as God.

visualMeditations.title: The Beast from the Sea
visualMeditations.image: Picture the dragon standing on the beach as the sea heaves. Out of the waves rises a monster — leopard's body, bear's feet, lion's jaws, seven heads, ten crowned horns, blasphemous names on every forehead. One head carries a terrible wound, now healed. All over the world, crowds gasp in admiration and bow.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The dragon gave him his power, his throne, and great authority” (v. 2). “They worshiped the beast, saying, ‘Who is like the beast? Who is able to make war with him?’” (v. 4). Every power that demands ultimate loyalty borrows its strength from the dragon.

visualMeditations.title: Given, Given, Given
visualMeditations.image: Picture the beast boasting and blaspheming, waging war on God's people — but notice, each time, a hand behind the scenes giving permission, setting a time limit: forty-two months, and not a day longer.
visualMeditations.meaning: “A mouth speaking great things and blasphemy was given to him. Authority to make war for forty-two months was given to him” (v. 5). The beast seems all-powerful, but everything he has is ‘given’, and his time is short.

visualMeditations.title: The Lamb-Like Dragon
visualMeditations.image: Picture a second beast, gentle-looking, with two small horns like a lamb. He works miracles, calls down fire, sets up a statue that seems to breathe and speak — and when he opens his mouth, you hear the voice of the dragon.
visualMeditations.meaning: “He had two horns like a lamb, and he spoke like a dragon” (v. 11). Not everything that looks like Jesus is from Jesus. Test what you hear by the voice, not the appearance.

visualMeditations.title: The Two Marks
visualMeditations.image: Picture two crowds. On one, the beast's stamp on hand and forehead — they can buy and sell freely. On the other, God's seal on their foreheads — shut out of the marketplace, but written in the Lamb's book of life.
visualMeditations.meaning: “That no one would be able to buy or to sell, unless he has that mark” (v. 17). Everyone bears someone's mark. Faithfulness to Christ may cost you in this world's marketplace; it will never cost you your place in the book of life (v. 8).

structure.label: The Beast from the Sea (v. 1-4)
structure.body: A beast rises from the sea with ten horns, seven heads, ten diadems and blasphemous names; it is like a leopard, bear and lion; the dragon gives it his power, throne and authority; one head seemed fatally wounded but was healed; the whole earth marvels and worships the dragon and the beast.

structure.label: Its War on the Saints (v. 5-10)
structure.body: The beast is given a mouth to blaspheme God, His name and His dwelling, and authority for forty-two months; it is allowed to make war on the saints and conquer them, and given authority over every nation; all whose names are not in the Lamb's book of life worship it; John calls for hearing, acceptance of captivity or death, and the endurance and faith of the saints.

structure.label: The Beast from the Land (v. 11-17)
structure.body: Another beast rises from the earth with two horns like a lamb but speaks like a dragon; it exercises the first beast's authority and makes the earth worship it; it performs great signs, even calling down fire; it deceives people into making an image of the first beast, gives the image breath to speak, and has those who refuse to worship killed; it forces everyone to receive a mark on the right hand or forehead, without which no one can buy or sell.

structure.label: The Number of the Beast (v. 18)
structure.body: This calls for wisdom: the one with understanding should calculate the number of the beast, for it is a human number — 666.

sections.heading: The Dragon's Allies
paragraphs: Chapter 12 ended with the dragon going off to make war on the woman's offspring. Chapter 13 shows his instruments: a beast from the sea and a beast from the land. Together with the dragon they form an unholy trinity — a counterfeit of the Father, the Son and the Spirit. The dragon gives his authority to the beast as the Father gives authority to the Son; the second beast leads people to worship the first as the Spirit leads people to worship Christ.

The first beast rises from the sea, like the four beasts of Daniel 7, which were four empires. It combines features of all four — leopard, bear and lion, with ten horns (v. 2). It is the sum of all the oppressive empires of history. For John's first readers it was clearly Rome: the empire across the sea, ruled by seven-headed succession, its emperors claiming blasphemous titles. But Rome is not the whole story; the beast reappears whenever a political power claims ultimate allegiance and persecutes God's people. Many also expect a final, personal embodiment of it before Christ's return, the ‘man of sin’ of 2 Thessalonians 2.

The beast is a parody of the Lamb. It has a head “wounded fatally” (v. 3) using the same word as the Lamb ‘slain’ (5:6), and it has a counterfeit resurrection: “His fatal wound was healed” (v. 3). The world is amazed and asks, “Who is like the beast? Who is able to make war with him?” (v. 4) — mocking the song of Moses, ‘Who is like you, LORD?’ The world worships power.

sections.heading: Here Is the Endurance of the Saints
paragraphs: The beast blasphemes and wars against God's people: “It was given to him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them” (v. 7). Notice how often the passive ‘was given’ appears (vv. 5, 7, 14, 15). The beast's authority is real but borrowed and limited — forty-two months (v. 5), the same short, fixed period as in chapters 11–12. God remains sovereign even over His enemies' power.

Who will worship the beast? “All who dwell on the earth... everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who has been killed” (v. 8). There are only two groups: those who belong to the earth and worship the beast, and those whose names are written in the Lamb's book. God's people are secure because they were known and chosen in Christ before the world began, as Paul says: “even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world” (Ephesians 1:4).

So what should believers do? “If anyone is to go into captivity, he will go into captivity. If anyone is to be killed with the sword, he must be killed. Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints” (v. 10). Not armed revolt, not compromise, but patient faithfulness. The saints overcome the beast not by taking up its sword but by refusing its worship, even at the cost of their lives (12:11).

sections.heading: The False Prophet
paragraphs: The second beast comes from the land. “He had two horns like a lamb, and he spoke like a dragon” (v. 11). He looks gentle and religious, but speaks Satan's words. Later he is called ‘the false prophet’ (16:13; 19:20). In John's world, he stood for the priests and councils of the imperial cult, who organised emperor-worship in every city of Asia and pressured Christians to burn incense to Caesar's image. In every age, he is religion and propaganda in the service of a godless state.

He does what religion should never do: he points people to the beast instead of to God. “He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast” (v. 12). He works miracles: “He performs great signs, even making fire come down out of the sky to the earth in the sight of people” (v. 13). Jesus warned, “For there will arise false christs, and false prophets, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones” (Matthew 24:24). Paul spoke of one “whose coming is according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders” (2 Thessalonians 2:9).

He sets up an image of the beast, gives it ‘breath’ so that it speaks, and orders the death of all who will not worship it (vv. 14–15). This is Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue all over again: bow, or burn. The faithful Christians of Asia faced exactly this choice.

sections.heading: The Mark and the Number
paragraphs: The false prophet forces everyone — small and great, rich and poor, free and slave — to receive “marks on their right hands, or on their foreheads; and that no one would be able to buy or to sell, unless he has that mark” (vv. 16–17). The mark is the beast's counterfeit of God's seal (7:3). The word χάραγμα was used for the emperor's stamp on coins and documents. The strongest reading is that the mark represents allegiance — what controls a person's thinking (forehead) and doing (hand). In Asia, refusing to honour Caesar and the guild gods could mean losing your trade. Some Christians expect a literal mark at the end; the principle holds either way: everyone bears someone's mark, and faithfulness to Christ may cost you economically.

Then the famous puzzle: “Here is wisdom. He who has understanding, let him calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man. His number is six hundred sixty-six” (v. 18). In Hebrew and Greek, letters doubled as numbers. The name ‘Nero Caesar’, spelled in Hebrew letters, adds up to 666; and some early manuscripts read 616, which matches the Latin spelling of the same name. This strongly suggests that John's first readers would have thought of Nero, the emperor who burned Christians in Rome, and the rumours that he would return.

But 666 is also symbolic. Seven is the number of completeness in Revelation; six falls short. 666 is six repeated three times: humanity's highest attempt to be God, always falling short. The beast is ‘the number of a man’ — however divine it claims to be, it is only human. Both meanings may be intended. The wisdom called for is not to decode the newest ruler, but to recognise every power that demands the worship belonging only to God — and to refuse it.

ntConnection.heading: The Man of Sin and the False Prophets
paragraphs: Paul described the same figure: “the man of sin is revealed, the son of destruction, he who opposes and exalts himself against all that is called God or that is worshiped; so that he sits as God in the temple of God, setting himself up as God” (2 Thessalonians 2:3–4). John wrote, “as you heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen” (1 John 2:18). The beast has many forerunners.
Jesus warned, “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves” (Matthew 7:15) — the beast with lamb's horns and a dragon's voice.

The New Testament teaches respect for governing authorities: “Let every soul be in subjection to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God” (Romans 13:1). But when the state demands worship, Peter and John's answer stands: “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, judge for yourselves” (Acts 4:19). Romans 13 and Revelation 13 belong together: the state is God's servant when it does good, and the dragon's beast when it claims to be God.

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “a dangerous animal.” θηρίον is a wild, savage beast, a predator. It is a deliberate contrast with ζῷον, the ‘living creatures’ around God's throne (4:6). The heavenly creatures lead worship of God; the beast demands worship for itself. In Daniel 7, empires are beasts and God's kingdom is given to ‘one like a son of man’ — human, as God intended. When rulers grasp at divinity, they become less than human: beasts.

Strong's: “a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue).” χάραγμα was used for the imperial seal on documents and the emperor's image on coins, and for brands on slaves and soldiers. It is the counterfeit of the σφραγίς, God's seal on His servants (7:3). Revelation presents only two options: God's seal or the beast's mark. The mark is ‘a badge of servitude’: it shows who owns you.

Strong's: “a likeness, i.e. (literally) statue, profile, or (figuratively) representation, resemblance.” εἰκών, from the image family, is a representation — a statue, a portrait, an image on a coin. Jesus held up a denarius and asked, ‘Whose image is this?’ Humans were made in God's image; Christ is ‘the image of the invisible God’ (Colossians 1:15). The beast's image is the great counterfeit: a man-made idol demanding the worship due to the true Image of God.

Strong's: “to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute.” ψηφίζω comes from ψῆφος, a pebble (the white stone of 2:17): counting by moving pebbles on a board. John invites the wise to ‘calculate’ — to work out what the number reveals. In the ancient practice of gematria, letters were numbers. But the call is for σοφία, wisdom, the moral discernment to see through the beast's claims, not for endless speculation about names.

Strong's: “vilification (especially against God).” βλασφημία is speech that slanders or insults — above all, speech that robs God of His honour. The beast's heads bear ‘blasphemous names’: titles like ‘lord’, ‘saviour’ and ‘son of god’ that belong to God and His Christ. Its mouth speaks great things and blasphemy. To claim divine honour for any human power is blasphemy, however patriotic it sounds.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit gives you eyes to recognise the beast — and the courage to refuse it.

items.title: Don't Be Impressed by Power
items.body: “The whole earth marveled at the beast” and asked, ‘Who is like the beast?’ (vv. 3–4). The Spirit warns you not to be dazzled by any power — political, economic, technological or cultural — that seems unstoppable. Only One is worthy of worship. Ask: ‘Who is like God?’

items.title: Test the Voice
items.body: The second beast looked like a lamb but spoke like a dragon (v. 11), and worked impressive signs (v. 13). The Spirit wants you to test every teacher, movement and miracle by one question: does it lead me to worship God and follow Jesus, or to serve something else?

items.title: Whose Mark Do You Bear?
items.body: Everyone carries someone's mark — in their thinking and in their doing (v. 16). The Spirit asks: whose name is written on your mind and your hands? If faithfulness costs you in the marketplace, remember your name is written in the Lamb's book of life.

audit.title: The Allegiance Check
audit.body: Is there any power — a nation, party, leader, employer or ideology — to which you give the loyalty that belongs only to God (v. 4)?

audit.title: The Deception Check
audit.body: Are you easily impressed by signs, success or charisma, without asking what they lead people to worship (vv. 13–14)?

audit.title: The Cost Check
audit.body: Would you be willing to lose income or opportunity rather than compromise your faith (v. 17)?

practices.title: Name the Beasts
practices.body: Write down the ‘beasts’ in your world — powers that demand ultimate allegiance and punish dissent. Then write beside each: ‘Its authority was given, and its time is short.’ Pray for courage to stay faithful, and for believers who live under oppressive regimes.

practices.title: Mark Your Mind and Hands
practices.body: Each morning this week, place your hand on your forehead and pray, ‘My mind belongs to Jesus,’ and then hold out your hands and pray, ‘My work belongs to Jesus.’ Let it remind you whose seal you bear (v. 16; 7:3).

prayerReflection: “Lord God, there is none like You. The world marvels at the beast and asks who can fight against it, but I know that all its power is borrowed and its time is short. Keep me from being impressed by any power that sets itself up in Your place. Give me wisdom to recognise the beast in every age, and discernment to hear the dragon's voice even when it comes from a lamb-like face. Keep me from the deception of false signs and false prophets. Thank You that my name is written in the Lamb's book of life, from the foundation of the world. Give me the endurance and faith of the saints, to refuse the beast's mark and worship, whatever it costs. Let Your seal be on my mind and on my hands. And strengthen my brothers and sisters who today face the choice to bow or die. In the name of the Lamb who was slain, Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Daniel's Four Beasts
storyConnections.summary: Daniel saw four great beasts rise from the stormy sea: a lion with eagle's wings, a bear, a leopard with four heads, and a terrifying fourth beast with iron teeth and ten horns, among which a little horn rose with a mouth speaking great things and made war on the saints ‘for a time, times, and half a time’. Then the Ancient of Days took His throne, the beast was destroyed, and the kingdom was given to one like a son of man and to the saints. Revelation's beast combines all four — and meets the same end.

storyConnections.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Golden Image
storyConnections.summary: King Nebuchadnezzar set up a huge golden image and commanded all peoples, nations and languages to fall down and worship it when the music sounded; whoever refused would be thrown into the fiery furnace. Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refused: ‘our God whom we serve is able to deliver us... But if not... we will not serve your gods, nor worship the golden image.’ They were thrown in — and a fourth figure walked with them in the fire. The image of the beast repeats Nebuchadnezzar's demand; the saints repeat their answer.

storyConnections.title: Polycarp Before the Proconsul
storyConnections.summary: Some sixty years after Revelation, Polycarp, the elderly bishop of Smyrna, was arrested and brought into the stadium. The Roman governor urged him to swear by the fortune of Caesar and say ‘Caesar is Lord’, and he would be set free. Polycarp replied that he had served Christ eighty-six years and Christ had never wronged him — how could he blaspheme his King who saved him? He was burned alive. He refused the beast's demand, and overcame by the word of his testimony.
